title: US chipmakers are getting crushed by a familiar source: AI jitters in Asia
excerpt: South Korea's KOSPI dropped more than 10% on Tuesday, with the index on track for its worst month in over 30 years. The volatility bled into US stocks.
content_html:
By Jennifer Sor

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

South Korea is once again dragging down the AI trade.

US chip stocks were in the red on Tuesday as Asian markets endured a heavy round of selling, particularly in shares of chips and memory makers. The result has been another bout of volatility hitting US chip stocks at a critical moment for the AI trade.

The jitters in the US market have followed a predictable pattern lately: South Korea's KOSPI sells off sharply overnight, triggering wider weakness in global tech stocks that hits the US market once trading kicks off.

The KOSPI dropped more than 10% on Tuesday, largely due to investors dumping shares of Samsung and SK Hynix, two memory giants that make up more than half of the index's total value. Buying of both stocks by Korean investors has also been fueled by heavy leverage, exacerbating the declines as margin calls force even more selling.

Samsung stock tumbled 13%, while SK Hynix shares listed in Korea plunged nearly 15% as investors rushed for the exit. US-listed ADRs of SK Hynix dropped 9% shortly after the opening bell in New York. The Nasdaq 100 fell nearly 2%.

Here's where US indexes stood shortly around 10:30 a.m. ET:

  • S&P 500: 7,400.96, down 0.16%
  • Dow Jones Industrial Average: 52,594.20, up 0.74% (+384.12 points)
  • Nasdaq 100: 27,555.49, down 1.73%

Here are some of the most notable moves in the chips and memory sectors:

  • SK Hynix (Korea-listed): -14%
  • Samsung: -13%
  • Micron: -9%
  • AMD: -8%
  • Marvell: -8%
  • Intel: -6%
  • Broadcom: -2%
  • Nvidia: -1%

South Korea's stock market has been exceptionally volatile this year after stellar gains in tech gave way to disorderly selling of the biggest winners. The KOSPI surged 110% through mid-June, but is down 33% from its peak. The index is on track for its worst month in more than 30 years, according to Jefferies.

Wall Street has been grasping for answers about what's behind the latest selling, with some analysts attributing the decline to investors rushing to take profits after a euphoric run-up in the AI trade.

David Morrison, a senior market analyst at Trade Nation, pointed to steep losses in Samsung and SK Hynix recently. SK Hynix's Korean shares are down 47% from their highs, while Samsung has dropped 38% from its peak. Neither stock is showing signs of a "significant rebound," he wrote in a note on Tuesday.

"There's an element of panic creeping in now," Morrison wrote. "Investors are exhibiting a lot of nervousness ahead of earnings reports from the major hyperscalers."

Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon will report second-quarter results this week, which has investors laser-focused on the AI narrative and whether firms will continue to double down on capex spending.

Economist David Rosenberg said the sell-off is rooted in concerns about Chinese competition in the AI race, something most investors weren't thinking about a month ago, he wrote this week.

JPMorgan's markets intelligence desk also said fears about Chinese competition are among the main drivers of the recent volatility.

Additionally, the bank pointed to the rotation going on in the the stock market as investors lean towards value stocks, as well as concerns related to the circular financing of AI. Investors also have "skepticism" about recent deals in the sector, such as Sandisk's partnership with Meta.

"I think people are just afraid/just want to sell tech/looking for excuses," Joshua Meyers, an executive director at JPMorgan, wrote in a note on Monday as the sell-off in Asia picked up steam. "Importantly, none of this seems fundamentally driven."

作者：Jennifer Sor 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

韩国再次拖累人工智能贸易。

由于亚洲市场遭遇一轮猛烈抛售，尤其是芯片和内存制造商的股票，美国芯片股周二出现下跌。 结果是，在人工智能行业的关键时刻，美国芯片股再次出现波动。

最近美国市场的紧张情绪遵循了一种可预见的模式：韩国综合股价指数隔夜大幅抛售，引发全球科技股普遍走软，一旦交易开始，美国市场就会受到影响。

KOSPI 周二下跌超过 10%，主要是由于投资者抛售三星和 SK 海力士的股票，这两家内存巨头的股价占该指数总价值的一半以上。 韩国投资者对这两只股票的购买也受到高杠杆率的推动，由于追加保证金要求迫使更多抛售，加剧了股价的下跌。

由于投资者纷纷撤离，三星股价暴跌 13%，而在韩国上市的 SK 海力士股价也暴跌近 15%。 纽约开盘后不久，SK 海力士在美国上市的 ADR 下跌了 9%。 纳斯达克100指数下跌近2%。

这是上午 10:30 左右美国指数的走势。 和：

  • S&P 500: 7,400.96, down 0.16%
  • 道琼斯工业平均指数：52,594.20，上涨0.74%（+384.12点）
  • 纳斯达克100：27,555.49，下跌1.73%

以下是芯片和内存领域的一些最引人注目的举措：

  • SK海力士（韩国上市）：-14%
  • 三星：-13%
  • 微米：-9%
  • AMD: -8%
  • 马维尔：-8%
  • Intel: -6%
  • 博通：-2%
  • 英伟达：-1%

今年，韩国股市异常波动，科技股的强劲涨幅被最大赢家的无序抛售所取​​代。 截至 6 月中旬，KOSPI 飙升 110%，但较峰值下跌 33%。 杰富瑞 (Jefferies) 表示，该指数有望迎来 30 多年来最糟糕的一个月。

华尔街一直在寻找最新抛售背后的原因，一些分析师将下跌归因于投资者在人工智能交易欣欣向荣后急于获利了结。

Trade Nation 高级市场分析师戴维·莫里森 (David Morrison) 指出，三星和 SK 海力士最近出现了大幅亏损。 SK 海力士的韩国股价较最高点下跌了 47%，而三星股价较最高点下跌了 38%。 他在周二的一份报告中写道，两只股票都没有显示出“显着反弹”的迹象。

莫里森写道：“现在恐慌情绪正在蔓延。” “在大型超大规模企业公布盈利报告之前，投资者表现出非常紧张的情绪。”

微软、Meta 和亚马逊将于本周公布第二季度业绩，投资者将重点关注人工智能的发展以及企业是否会继续加倍资本支出。

经济学家戴维·罗森伯格(David Rosenberg)本周写道，他表示，抛售的根源在于对中国在人工智能竞赛中竞争的担忧，这是大多数投资者一个月前没有想到的。

摩根大通市场情报部门还表示，对中国竞争的担忧是近期波动的主要驱动因素之一。

此外，该银行指出，随着投资者倾向于价值股，股市正在发生轮动，以及与人工智能循环融资相关的担忧。 投资者对该行业最近的交易也持“怀疑”态度，例如Sandisk与Meta的合作。

“我认为人们只是害怕/只是想出售科技/寻找借口，”摩根大通执行董事约书亚·迈耶斯(Joshua Meyers)周一在一份报告中写道，亚洲股市抛售势头加剧。 “重要的是，这一切似乎都不是根本驱动的。”
